Welcome
Safeguarding
Welcome to Ormiston Beachcroft Academy
We are an inclusive alternative provision based in the heart of Westminster, where every young person is valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. At Ormiston Beachcroft, we believe that together, everyone achieves more. We are proud to be rated a Good school by Ofsted (2024), reflecting the hard work of our staff, the progress of our students, and the strength of our school community.
Latest News
Safeguarding
We pride ourselves on ensuring that all pupils are able to learn in an environment which is both safe and supportive, whilst recognising the individual needs of all our pupils.
Ofsted
The latest Ofsted inspection was in April 2024 and the Academy was judged to be good.

View details of our school day, provision for before and afterschool, uniform, school meals and our timetable.

Leaders and staff develop good working relationships with pupils. Consequently, pupils make positive progress in their learning and behaviour.

British Values
SMSC and British Values
At Beachcroft Academy, Social, Moral, Spiritual and Cultural (SMSC) development and the promotion of British Values are embedded throughout the curriculum and enriched through a wide range of extracurricular opportunities.
Within lessons, SMSC and British Values are reflected through the language modelled by staff, the challenging of misconceptions, and the careful selection of topics and texts that broaden learners’ understanding of different cultures, communities and perspectives. For example, Key Stage 3 Mathematics explores travel and currency, while Refugee Boy is studied as a set text in Key Stage 3 English.
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education is delivered to all year groups through the Votes4Schools programme. To improve attendance and engagement, PSHE lessons have been re-timetabled to a different part of the school day, having previously all taken place during Period 1. This change has led to improved participation and learner engagement.
Our commitment to SMSC and British Values is further strengthened through a broad enrichment programme. All learners have access to enrichment opportunities within their timetable, including (but not limited to) PanArts, Music Club, Off-site PE at local leisure centres, Cooking Club, Games Club and Art Club.
We also offer a range of educational visits as part of our wider curriculum. These have included visits to Mary Seacole’s grave site, the British Museum, Science Museum, Natural History Museum, Imperial War Museum, the Unicorn Theatre and the Roundhouse.
Key cultural and social events are celebrated across the school through assemblies and social times. These include World Food Day, where learners and staff cook and share cultural dishes, Black History Month (including collaborative dance projects, storytelling around Anansi, assemblies and trips), Remembrance Day, Red for Anti-Racism Day, Autism Awareness Month, and many more opportunities to promote understanding, respect and inclusion.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our mission at Beachcroft Academy is Together Everyone Achieves More. This ethos underpins everything we do and is reflected in our core values, which are built upon four key principles: Trust, Excellence, Ambition and Motivation. We are a community founded on trust, committed to excellence in all aspects of school life, ambitious in our aspirations for every learner, and motivated to ensure that all can succeed.
Guided by these values, we are committed to developing both currency and character in our learners. We ensure that every learner achieves meaningful qualifications that enhance future life chances, while also nurturing the personal qualities, resilience and social understanding needed to thrive as confident, responsible individuals in modern Britain.
We use necessary cookies to keep this site working and optional statistics cookies to understand site usage.
Our Academy
Vision and Values

Welcome
I am extremely proud to welcome you to Ormiston Beachcroft Academy. We are an alternative provision based in Westminster, and we are committed to motivating, supporting and inspiring pupils to re-engage with their education. We aim to provide every pupil with a high standard of education, which sets them up for successful futures. Our dedicated team of specialist staff aim to provide a broad and balanced education that goes beyond the academic, and aims to develop the whole person – responsible, reflective young people that are able to fulfil their potential.
Beachcroft is buzzing with positive attitudes and behaviour, and is a place where staff inspire and support all learners to be the best that they can be. We are a small academy, which allows to us really get to know our pupils and their families, building strong, positive working relationships. At Beachcroft, we are like a family, and we encourage our pupils, families and wider community to be actively involved in academy life. We are proud of our small community and proud of how we work together as a family. We have an excellent record of ensuring that all our young people reach a positive destination, whether that be college, apprenticeships or employment.
Our ethos is based around the Ormiston Academies Trust’s vision of “Achieving More Together.” Every person in our academy should feel valued, and our key expectations are to be safe, be respectful and be ready to learn. We take great pride in our academy, from how inclusive and welcoming we are, through to uniform and conduct, and we encourage our pupils to take ownership of this, and consider what positive change looks like for them. Every pupil has their own journey that they are on, and we will give each of them our very best in supporting them along that journey.

Inspiring Drama Workshops with the University of West London
In the week following half term, we were delighted to host a series of engaging Drama workshops for our KS3 students in partnership with the University of West London. Pupils have been working collaboratively with undergraduate students to develop a piece of Theatre in Education, providing a powerful platform for pupil voice within the wider community. Throughout the workshops, students demonstrated enthusiasm, creativity and maturity, fully immersing themselves in the process. They are thoroughly enjoying the experience and are eagerly anticipating their final performances, we look forward to sharing updates soon!

pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
The PE and Sport Premium is government funding provided to primary schools to improve the quality, provision, and participation in physical education and sport. The funding is used to ensure that all pupils develop healthy, active lifestyles and have access to a broad range of sporting opportunities, both within and beyond the school day.
At Ormiston Beachcroft Academy, the PE and Sport Premium is used strategically to enhance the PE curriculum, increase opportunities for extra-curricular sport, and promote physical and mental wellbeing for all pupils. A key focus is encouraging lifelong participation in physical activity while ensuring inclusive access for all learners, including those with additional needs.
How the funding is used
The PE and Sport Premium supports:
Impact of the funding
The funding has had a positive impact on pupil engagement and participation in physical activity. Pupils across the academy regularly take part in structured PE lessons, enrichment activities, and daily physical play. Participation levels have increased, particularly for vulnerable pupils and those with high needs, supporting improvements in confidence, wellbeing, and physical development.
Through the use of external providers, specialist equipment, and varied sporting environments, pupils have been able to broaden their sporting experiences and develop a positive attitude towards health and fitness. The academy continues to build on this success to ensure high-quality PE and sport provision for all learners.

Praise for students following GCSE results day
Ormiston Beachcroft Academy is recognising the achievements, progress and resilience of its Year 11 students on GCSE results day.
Our school is celebrating the achievements of its students, who have shown resilience and ambition throughout their studies and are now preparing to take their next steps in education, training or employment.
This year’s cohort achieved particularly highly in GCSE history, and BTEC home cooking skills. There were several successes, including 16 grade 4+ or equivalent qualifications, including grade 5s in English language, mathematics and fine art, and a grade 6 in history.
The whole school community has come together today to mark the students’ achievements, hard work and dedication, as they look ahead to the next stage of their education.
While all students have achieved well, some individual achievements include:
Ormiston Beachcroft Academy is an alternative provision supporting and inspiring students to re-engage with their education. As part of Ormiston, the school is dedicated to providing the highest quality education and ensuring that every child, regardless of their background, gains the skills and opportunities they need to thrive.
Michelle Burgess-Allen, Principal at Ormiston Beachcroft Academy, said:
“This is a fantastic day for our students and the wider school community. These results reflect their ambition, perseverance and positive approach, alongside the tireless work of our staff team.
“We are enormously proud of each student and look forward to seeing them continue to flourish as they take their next steps.”

Curriculum Overview
It is sometimes assumed that qualifications achieved in an Alternative Provision (AP) setting are different from those gained in mainstream schools. This is not the case. Students studying in AP complete the same qualifications, sit the same examinations, and meet the same coursework requirements as students in mainstream education. The expectations for effort, commitment and achievement remain equally high.
At Ormiston Beachcroft Academy, our curriculum is designed to provide a balanced and engaging learning experience. It combines academic study with creative, practical and physical subjects so that students can develop a wide range of knowledge and skills while working towards their future goals.
Our core subjects include English Language, English Literature, Maths, and Science (Double Award), and Core Physical Education, which form the foundation of every student’s programme of study. Upon admission, pupils are given the opportunity to select their option subjects from three option blocks. This structure allows students to choose three subjects that best support their interests, strengths, and future pathway aspirations.
Alongside these core subjects, students also study a range of option subjects that allow them to explore their interests and develop practical and creative skills. Current subjects available include Art, Computing and Computer Science, Business, and Home Cooking Skills.
This curriculum is designed to give students a broad and balanced education, enabling them to gain recognised qualifications while developing practical skills and confidence for further education, training or employment.

SEND at Ormiston Beachcroft Academy
Click here for our SEND policy.
Detailed information regarding our provision for pupils with SEND can be found here. We hope parents of current and prospective students find this information helpful and we encourage all interested parties to contact the academy for more information.
In addition, we offer the following provisions:
Breakfast club
Every day before school, we have a Breakfast club which gives pupils the opportunity for a “soft landing” for the day and a opportunity to catch up with staff, as well as have a full breakfast.
Small group work
Some of our pupils will take part in withdrawal intervention to complete tasks in small groups or even one-to-one with a member of the SEND team. We work really hard to make sure that each pupil is achieving their best and are not hindered by any learning needs.
These sessions may include mentoring, literacy intervention, lego therapy or more
We also run a range of sessions focusing on supporting pupils with their social, emotional and mental health needs.

Ofsted
Ofsted Inspection – April 2024
We are pleased to share the outcome of our most recent Ofsted inspection, which took place in April 2024. We are delighted that Ormiston Beachcroft Academy continues to be graded ‘Good’ in all areas.
Inspectors were particularly impressed by the strength of our school community, noting that:
“Typically, pupils describe the school community as being like a family. Teachers are knowledgeable and explain things clearly. Pupils produce high quality work.”
We are proud of this recognition, which reflects the hard work and dedication of our students, staff, and wider school community.
You can read the full report here:Ofsted – Ormiston Beachcroft Academy
Parent Feedback – Ofsted Parent View
Since schools now receive just 24 hours’ notice before an Ofsted inspection, there is limited opportunity to gather parental feedback during the inspection period itself. Instead, Ofsted collects ongoing parent feedback through their Parent View platform.
We encourage all parents and carers to share their views. If you are pleased with the work of the school, we would be grateful for your positive feedback. If you do have concerns, we kindly ask that you speak to us directly in the first instance, so we can work together to resolve any issues.
You can access the Parent View platform here:Parent view

Pupil Premium
Information on how Ormiston Beachcroft supports disadvantaged learners through the Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is a government-funded initiative that allocates additional resources to schools and academies to support pupils who are eligible for free school meals. This funding is intended to help reduce barriers to learning and improve educational outcomes for pupils from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Although the funding is targeted at particular groups, the approaches developed through Pupil Premium provision often have a positive impact across the wider school community.
At Ormiston Beachcroft, promoting fairness, inclusion, and high-quality outcomes for all learners is a key priority. We are committed to ensuring that every pupil has access to a broad, age-appropriate curriculum, alongside meaningful enrichment opportunities that support both academic progress and personal development. Where appropriate, this also includes supporting pupils to successfully re-engage with mainstream education. Pupil Premium funding is used strategically to narrow achievement gaps, raise aspirations, strengthen confidence, and improve long-term life chances.
Our support includes a range of practical and targeted interventions, such as access to a free breakfast club, assistance with school uniform, reading intervention programmes, social and emotional assessments, and close collaboration with statutory and voluntary agencies. Alongside this, we provide a varied enrichment offer designed to develop pupils’ cultural capital and wider experiences.
Further details can be found in the document below, which outlines our Pupil Premium strategy, including key priorities, planned actions, anticipated impact, and the challenges faced by some of the most disadvantaged pupils in the borough.
